... is an understatement for the artistic tricks Daniel Huffman shares in his [current post][post] 
on the [Something About Maps blog][blog]. The techniques shown encompass the treatment of the shaded 
relief, label brackets, blurs and glows, line generalisation, and more (many of which are detailled 
further in other posts on the blog).

While I am involved in the production of "analytical maps"[^analytical] (if any) rather than very 
professional cartography products, this [post][post] is an impressive treasure trove of advanced 
cartographic techniques.

[![Blurs and glows (on the right) aid readability of labels and other map elements (source: Daniel Huffman)](blurs-and-glows.png "Blurs and glows (on the right) aid readability of labels and other map elements (source: Daniel Huffman)")][post]

If this kind of article interests you, I also recommend another recent post by Daniel, titled "[On
sin][post2]" . While it touches on the somewhat simmering AI "controversy" of the ICA[^ica] Commission on
Map Design (which I chose not to cover here), that is not the focal point of that post.

[^analytical]: For lack of a better term. What I mean is: limited effort functional and pragmatic
maps that usually serve an analytical end.
[^ica]: The International Cartographic Association is an organisation formed of national member
organisations, to provide a forum for issues and techniques in cartography and geographic
information science.

[post]: https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/2026/08/03/a-few-minor-niceties/
